 Before Ii Addl. Jmfc Court, Sirsi For The Alleged
 Offence P/U/S 59(i) Of Food Safety And Standards Act,
 To Meet The Ends Of Justice. 
 This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
 The Court Made The Following:
 -2-
 Nc: 2024:Khc-D:3445
 Crl.P No. 102338 of 2023
 Order
1. This petition is filed challenging the initiation of the criminal proceedings for commission of an alleged offence under Section 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("the Act" for short). 
2. It is the specific contention of the petitioner that the statutory rule requires that the report of the Food Analyst be dispatched within 14 days. The Form-B, which is produced Annexure-D indicates that the sample was received by the designated Officer on 24.07.2019 for analysis and the same was analyzed between 05.08.2019 and 08.08.2019 and thereafter, the report was stated to have been prepared on 08.08.2019 itself.
3. This report though dated 08.08.2019 is stated to have been dispatched on 17.08.2019 and ultimately sent by registered post on 20.08.2019 as per the photocopy of the postal receipt produced by the learned Additional Government Advocate. 
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3445 4. It is clear from the above that, the report which has to be dispatched within 14 days i.e., on or before 14.08.2019 was dispatched nearly a week thereafter on 20.08.2019. Since the statutory period for sending the report has not been adhered to, the entire proceedings would stand vitiated. 
5. Consequently, the proceedings are quashed. Accordingly, the petition is allowed. 
Sd/-
